_about: Bidirectional interactions between host SEX HORMONES (estradiol, progesterone,
testosterone) and bacteria - a dimension neither seed_data.json (condition ->
taxon) nor cross_feeding.json (bacterium -> bacterium) captures.
The mind-blowing idea: this is not a one-way street. Bacteria do not merely
respond to host hormone levels; some USE host steroids as growth factors,
and others CATABOLIZE them - so the microbiota is both an audience for and an
editor of the host's hormonal state. The cross-talk is strongest in mucosal
environments (oral cavity, gut).
NATURAL vs SYNTHETIC matters (see hi_natural_vs_synthetic): gut bacteria
rapidly metabolize the body's own bioidentical steroids but largely resist
synthetic analogues (progestins, ethinylestradiol, 17-alkylated androgens),
so an effect shown for a natural hormone should NOT be assumed for its
synthetic drug form.
direction field:
hormone->bacterium : the host steroid changes the bacterium (growth, biofilm)
bacterium->hormone : the bacterium chemically changes the steroid (catabolism)
site field: where the interaction is demonstrated - oral cavity vs gut matters,
the same rank/site discipline the rest of this atlas uses.
IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: much of the Prevotella evidence is in-vitro at
supraphysiological hormone concentrations. Read this as a mechanistic map of
what CAN happen, not proof it dominates in vivo.

interactions.tldr: TLDR: oral Prevotella can use your estrogen and progesterone as a growth 'vitamin' (vitamin-K substitute).
interactions.effect: Prevotella intermedia (formerly Bacteroides melaninogenicus subsp. intermedius) requires vitamin K (naphthoquinones) for electron transport; it can substitute estradiol or progesterone for vitamin K, so host sex steroids let it grow where vitamin K is scarce.
interactions.note: The classic result. Growth curves showed B. melaninogenicus subsp. intermedius and subsp. melaninogenicus - but NOT B. gingivalis - could substitute progesterone or estradiol for vitamin K, taking up 2.6-5.4 x 10^-4 umol of steroid per ug cell protein. This is the leading mechanistic explanation for pregnancy gingivitis: rising progesterone/estradiol feed Prevotella at the gumline.

interactions.tldr: TLDR: estrogen and progesterone can thicken Prevotella's biofilm and boost its growth.
interactions.effect: Estradiol regulates planktonic growth, coaggregation, polysaccharide production and biofilm formation of the Prevotella intermedia group (P. intermedia, P. nigrescens, P. pallens) - enhancing the physiological activity and biofilm of specific Prevotella groups.
interactions.note: Effects differ by species and are concentration-dependent, so this is 'enhances specific groups', not a blanket 'more Prevotella'. A separate saliva-derived oral-biofilm model found progesterone and estradiol raised PROTEOLYTIC activity to levels comparable with menadione (vitamin K) supplementation - consistent with the vitamin-K-substitution mechanism operating in a mixed community - though that study found no overall shift in biofilm composition (PMID 37621393).
interactions.ref: Yokoyama et al. 2014, Anaerobe/Arch Oral Biol - estradiol & Prevotella intermedia group biofilm (PMID 24594108)

interactions.tldr: TLDR: Prevotella can break your progesterone and estrogen down, clearing them locally.
interactions.effect: Prevotella species possess genes and hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (HSD) enzymes that catabolize/degrade steroid hormones (progesterone, pregnenolone, estradiol), modifying their chemical structure and participating in local or systemic hormonal clearance.
interactions.note: The return leg that makes the relationship bidirectional: the same bacteria that eat host steroids for growth also chemically transform them. Balance between steroid uptake and breakdown is mediated by HSDs. This sits inside a broader gut-bacterial steroid-metabolism story (see hi_gut_reductases_progesterone).
interactions.ref: Mechanistic context reviewed in Siddiqui et al. 2022, Biology 11(11):1683 (PMID 36421397); HSD/steroid-metabolism enzymology in gut bacteria: Nature Communications 2025 (PMID 40628728)

interactions.tldr: TLDR: gut bacteria chemically convert your progesterone (e.g. into 5-beta-dihydroprogesterone) - and these enzymes are commoner in women.
interactions.effect: Common human gut bacteria encode Delta4-3-ketosteroid 5-beta-reductase, 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase/Delta5-4 isomerase and Delta6-3-ketosteroid reductase enzyme families; a Delta4-3-ketosteroid 5-beta-reductase reduces progesterone to 5-beta-dihydroprogesterone in the gut.
interactions.note: Broadens the Prevotella-specific picture to the whole gut community: the microbiome is a genuine node in steroid metabolism, not just a bystander. Notably these enzymes are ENRICHED IN FEMALES over males in metagenomes - a possible microbial contributor to sex differences in steroid handling. Connects to this app's Progesterone condition (Gordonibacter/Eggerthella producing progestins from glucocorticoids, PMID 38795705) - production and reduction are two ends of the same microbial steroid-metabolism axis.
interactions.ref: Identification of gut bacteria reductases that biotransform steroid hormones, Nature Communications 2025 (PMID 40628728)

interactions.tldr: TLDR: gut bacteria digest your body's OWN (bioidentical) hormones fast, but mostly ignore synthetic drug versions - so a microbiome effect proven for natural hormone may not carry over to the pill.
interactions.mechanism: natural vs synthetic: differential bacterial metabolism
interactions.effect: Gut bacteria rapidly metabolize NATURAL/bioidentical steroids but RESIST synthetic analogues. Natural progesterone was completely degraded in ~2 h (half-life 28 min), while the synthetic progestins medroxyprogesterone acetate (half-life 644 min; >12% intact at 24 h) and levonorgestrel (half-life 240 min) resisted degradation ~10-fold. Structural modifications (C17 acetylation, C6 methyl, ethinyl groups) make synthetics poor substrates for microbial enzymes. Synthetic estrogen (ethinylestradiol) is likewise structurally hardened versus natural estradiol, and 17-alkylated synthetic androgens resist metabolism versus natural testosterone (the 'testobolome').
interactions.note: WHY IT MATTERS for this app: the progesterone->Bifidobacterium boost, the Prevotella growth effects, and the reductase biotransformations above were all demonstrated with NATURAL hormones, which bacteria actually engage with. Synthetic progestins/estrogens/androgens largely pass the microbiome by, so those effects should NOT be assumed for the drug forms. This is a mechanism (differential metabolism), not a head-to-head microbiome-outcome trial - nobody has directly compared, say, bioidentical progesterone vs a progestin on Bifidobacterium abundance, so 'synthetic doesn't boost Bifidobacterium' is a well-grounded expectation, not a measured fact.
interactions.ref: Progestogens Are Metabolized by the Gut Microbiota, Pharmaceutics 2020 (PMID 32806503); estrogen: OCs shift gut microbiota, Nutrients 2025 (PMID 40871620); testosterone: the testobolome, npj Biofilms Microbiomes 2025 (PMID 41513699)
